name: Perplexity
summary: Perplexity is an AI search product that answers queries with web-grounded synthesized responses and numbered source citations, offered via a consumer web/app product and a developer API platform.

product.one_liner: AI search product that returns web-grounded answers with source citations
product.description: Perplexity provides a public web and app search/answer interface. Official Help Center and getting-started materials describe real-time web search, summarized answers, and numbered citations linking to sources. Paid individual plans (Pro, Max) are listed on the official pricing page. Developer documentation describes an API platform with Agent, Search, and Embeddings APIs for web-grounded answers, ranked search results, and embeddings.
key_capabilities: real-time web search with synthesized answers
numbered citations / source transparency in answers
consumer web and mobile search/answer product
subscription tiers (Free, Pro, Max) on public pricing
Agent API for web-grounded answers and tool-enabled model access
Search API for ranked web results
Embeddings API for semantic search / RAG pipelines

market.primary_persona: Consumers, knowledge workers, and developers building search or research features
market.problem: Users want timely answers drawn from the live web with visible sources, rather than navigating only ranked links or uncited chat responses

business_model.notes: Public pricing lists Free ($0/month), Pro ($20/month), and Max ($200/month) for individuals, with Enterprise plan surfaces on the same pricing hub. Developer APIs are documented separately; usage billing details for API are not fully transcribed in this entry.

ai_profile.model_strategy: Product and API docs emphasize web-grounded answering and search infrastructure; Agent API documentation also describes access to third-party models (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI) with web search tools. Help Center mentions selectable third-party models for Pro Search. Proprietary model details are not fully specified in the primary docs used here.
ai_profile.data_advantage: Advantage depends on retrieval quality, citation UX, and query/feedback loops; extent of proprietary index or model advantage is not fully public in attached sources
ai_profile.notes: AI capability is structural: without model-backed synthesis plus retrieval, the product collapses to conventional search links or a thin wrapper. Removing either search grounding or generative answering removes the core offering.

traction.notes: No query volume, MAU, ARR, or hiring metrics are included. Secondary press figures and Wikipedia traffic claims are omitted from traction signals. product_led is not claimed: self-serve signup exists, but PLG expansion mechanics are not evidenced beyond direct web access.

funding.notes: Secondary sources report multiple large rounds and valuations with conflicting figures. Numeric fields remain null until a dated primary or high-quality single snapshot is attached.

product.rationale: Judgment: coherent AI search product with documented citations, clear consumer surface, and documented API surfaces. Strong for the category, not exceptional packaging beyond peers.

market.rationale: Judgment: AI search is a clear, active category with identifiable same-category peers. Capped at 4: no independent category-level demand report attached (company materials alone cannot justify 5).

business_model.rationale: Judgment: public Free plus paid Pro/Max tiers and Enterprise surfaces provide a concrete mixed monetization path; API monetization is documented as a platform but not fully priced in this entry.

technology.rationale: Judgment (application layer): meaningful search + LLM orchestration and API platform work versus AI-search peers; not scored as a frontier model lab. Within-layer frame only.

growth.rationale: Not scored: no sourced query volume, seats, or revenue metrics attached in this entry.

competitive_position.rationale: Judgment (application layer): visible AI-search contender versus same-category peers (e.g. You.com); relative share and defensibility not measured. Traditional search and major chatbot assistants are treated as adjacent substitutes, not peer-set equals.
